rows.subtype: Hiding behind a parent at a party [Actor]
rows.description: A child clings to a parent's leg and refuses to greet anyone; staying away from the scary thing feels like relief, and gentle nearness helps more than pushing.

rows.subtype: Approach: avoiding reminders and refusing to talk [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teen puts away every photo and leaves the room when the person is mentioned, hoping the pain will vanish, but avoidance keeps it sharp and distances him from family who want to share.

rows.subtype: Friend all good then all bad [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager describes a friend as perfect one week and as a total traitor the next after a small slight; strong feelings make it hard to hold both good and disappointing sides together.
A child proposes turns, splitting time or trading choices, such as "You pick this game, I pick the next". Compromise works when both sides feel heard and the deal is remembered.

rows.subtype: Restless and asking what to do [Actor]
rows.description: A child declares boredom after ten minutes and wants a screen; boredom is uncomfortable but can also be the doorway to imagination when adults give time and simple materials.
A preschooler wanders, whines or asks what can I do when nothing holds attention. Boredom is a cue to offer or make choices, and some boredom builds creativity.
